facts.raw_span: A man in his 40s presented with a 2-year history of multiple asymptomatic lesions on the face and neck
The lesions were round, hypopigmented macules and were symmetrically distributed in the affected area
The macules had appeared on his cheeks 2 years earlier and had gradually coalesced
The size of the lesions ranged from approximately 2 to 3 mm to 25 mm in diameter
There was no hair growth at the site of the lesions
He was previously treated for tinea versicolor, without success
Histopathologic findings showed plate-like subepidermal tumor extending horizontally under epidermis with multiple cord-like connections to overlying epidermis
Neoplastic cords consisted of clear/pale epithelial cells with cytoplasm showing strong periodic acid-Schiff staining due to glycogen accumulation
Stroma formed by fibrous connective tissue
Marked elastosis observed in dermis surrounding tumor
Multiple round, hypopigmented macules symmetrically distributed on face and neck
Lesions ranged from 2-3 mm to 25 mm in diameter
Absence of hair growth in affected areas
